questions.q: What is the most important sign that a chemical change has occurred?
questions.a: The formation of a new substance with different properties is the key sign. If a student says "a change in shape," they are likely confusing physical changes with chemical changes.

questions.q: If you melt an ice cube into water, is this a chemical change? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is not a chemical change because the water is still water (H2O), just in a different state. If the student says "yes," they are failing to recognize that no new substance was created.

questions.q: A baker heats sugar until it turns into a brown, sweet-smelling liquid called caramel. Can this be reversed to get the original white sugar crystals back?
questions.a: No, it cannot be reversed because the heat caused a chemical change, creating a new substance (caramel). If the student thinks it can be reversed by cooling, they misunderstand that chemical changes are usually permanent.

questions.q: Compare burning a candle wick to melting the candle wax. Which one is more likely to be a chemical change?
questions.a: Burning the wick is a chemical change because it reacts with oxygen to produce smoke and ash, whereas melting the wax is a physical change. Students often struggle to see that a single object can undergo both types of changes at once.

questions.q: Is it possible for a chemical change to occur without heat? Provide an example.
questions.a: Yes, rusting of iron occurs at room temperature when iron reacts with oxygen and moisture. If a student answers "no," they believe that chemical changes always require fire or high heat.

questions.q: Think of a kitchen activity. Describe a process where you mix two things and a chemical change happens.
questions.a: Baking a cake is a great example, as the batter (flour, eggs, sugar) changes into a solid, spongy structure through heat. A poor answer would be "mixing salt and water," because that is just a mixture, not a chemical change.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A chemical change is a process in which one or more substances undergo a ______ to create entirely new substances with different properties.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered why a piece of ______ turns into ash when it burns, but simply turns into smaller pieces when you rip it?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to distinguish between physical and chemical changes by identifying whether a new substance with unique properties has been created.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Have you ever ______ why a piece of paper turns into ash when it burns, but simply turns into smaller pieces when you rip it?
